title: A custom after an abrupt change

captions.energy: Hurrying the rejection of former routines
captions.emotions: Seeking peace through understanding the change

meaning: Domestic customs support renewal when ending the familiar leaves time to understand what you actually want to preserve.
text: Feeling at home may rest on recognisable actions: a familiar evening, a shared table and your way of preparing for the week. The Hierophant in the physical position of Muladhara describes maintaining this form. Death in energy tests your footing through rejecting the old too sharply: change should be immediate and leave nothing behind. The Hermit in emotions seeks considered peace and understanding of what matters to two people. Outward decisiveness therefore need not match inward readiness, especially when small sustaining habits disappear alongside unnecessary work.

For example, you decide to simplify weekends and cancel the previous domestic lunch completely. More time is free, but a familiar meeting point is missing. **Removing unnecessary work does not mean abandoning a custom’s whole meaning.** Brief tea together can preserve something important without restoring the old load. Reflection helps select what truly supports home instead of requiring the entire former routine to be accepted or rejected again.

The difficulty is treating a wish to preserve something familiar as an attempt to go backwards. Personal understanding retreats further into silence while the new order still feels alien. Ending an old form does not automatically make its replacement lived in. Peace comes closer when change allows meaningful continuity and a small familiar meeting is not regarded as an obstacle to renewal. Shared life can then remain recognisable as it changes.
